description: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (BCM2711) single-board computer, 1-8GB RAM, gigabit ethernet, USB3, microSD3.0. Runs OpenWrt, Ubuntu Server, Raspberry Pi OS. Boots from SD, USB mass storage, or network (EEPROM bootloader).

hardware.usb: 2x USB 3.0, 2x USB 2.0 (VIA VL805 controller, USB-C OTG support)
hardware.storage: microSD (DSLI mode), USB mass storage, netboot; NVMe only via PCIe HAT boards
hardware.power: USB-C 5.1V/3A (official PSU). Bus-powered 2.5in HDDs can brown out weak PSUs — use externally powered disks
hardware.serial: GPIO14/15 UART, 115200 8N1, 3.3V. Silent unless BOOT_UART=1 (bootloader) or console enabled (kernel). Pi 5 uses a dedicated 3-pin debug connector instead
hardware.eeprom: 64Mbit SPI flash (W25Q64) holds the bootloader. Update flows: SD/USB recovery files, network (TFTP), or on-device rpi-eeprom-update
hardware.note: Board recovery: nRPIBOOT jumper (GPIO40) + rpiboot mass-storage gadget gives the host direct block-device access over USB-C — no boot media or network required

boot.chain: BCM2711 ROM -> EEPROM bootloader (SPI) -> boot medium. Bootloader reads config.txt / kernel from FAT boot partition (SD, USB) or fetches them over TFTP (network).

boot_order.semantics: BOOT_ORDER nibbles are tried RIGHT to LEFT. 0xf142 = network (2), usb (4), sd (1), then restart (f).

examples.0xf142: network -> USB -> SD -> restart (LAN-first management policy)

netboot_protocol.dhcp: DISCOVER with vendor-class option 60 = PXEClient:Arch:00000:UNDI:002001, option 93/94/97 (ARCH/NDI/GUID). GUID embeds ASCII Rpi4 or Rpi5 plus the MAC.
netboot_protocol.requirements: OFFER must include option 66 (TFTP server) and/or 67 (bootfile) or the bootloader ignores it and keeps DISCOVERing forever. Plain DHCP OFFERs without boot options are rejected.
netboot_protocol.transport: TFTP only (no HTTP boot on BCM2711/2712). Requests <serial>/ first, then root. dnsmasq with enable-tftp + per-host dhcp-option 66/67 is sufficient.
netboot_protocol.tftp_files: config.txt, start4.elf/start5.elf, fixup*.dat, kernel*.img, dtbs, initramfs — same files as a FAT boot partition.

eeprom_update.files: recovery.bin + pieeprom.upd + pieeprom.sig placed on the BOOT MEDIUM (SD/USB FAT partition) or the TFTP root. The bootloader compares versions and applies once.
eeprom_update.signature: pieeprom.sig = sha256 of pieeprom.upd + ts line (generated by rpi-eeprom-digest or scripts/pi_eeprom.py). Verified by recovery.bin.

netboot-rescue.description: Arm an on-demand TFTP rescue server on an OpenWrt router (dnsmasq + rescue kernel + busybox initramfs with telnetd). Any network-fallback Pi boots a RAM-only rescue shell over LAN. scripts/pi_netboot.py arm/disarm is the network-boot on/off switch.
netboot-rescue.requires: OpenWrt router with root SSH on the same L2, rescue boot tree, Pi MAC

tested_hardware.notes: Full rescue executed: netboot-looping Pi (dead boot medium + network-first EEPROM) recovered to a RAM shell via dnsmasq TFTP on the lab router; EEPROM config fixed over the same channel.

usb-image.description: Write an OS image (Ubuntu Server, Raspberry Pi OS, OpenWrt) to a USB disk / SD card and boot it natively. conwrt pi_image.py provisions a Pi-attached disk over SSH; scripts/pi_rescue/flash-rescue.sh writes a local stick. Headless via cloud-init (user-data/network-config/meta-data on the boot FAT) or Raspberry Pi OS boot-marker + authorized_keys injection.
usb-image.requires: Pi with USB-MSD-capable EEPROM (all 2020+ bootloaders), writable medium

tested_hardware.notes: Ubuntu Server 26.04.1 arm64+raspi written to a Pi-attached 1TB USB disk from the netboot rescue shell, cloud-init injected via vfat mount, first boot verified over SSH.

eeprom-update-netboot.description: Deliver EEPROM config/firmware changes over the network: build a package with scripts/pi_eeprom.py (BOOT_ORDER, BOOT_UART, etc.) and place recovery.bin + pieeprom.upd + pieeprom.sig in the netboot tree or on the boot medium. The bootloader applies it on the next boot and skips re-application on version match.
eeprom-update-netboot.requires: netboot tree (armed rescue server) OR writable boot FAT; no signed-boot OTP lock

tested_hardware.notes: BOOT_ORDER changed 0xf241 -> 0xf142 (network-first) via TFTP-delivered update; verified by subsequent netboot-first behavior.

rpiboot-usb.description: Physical recovery/provisioning over USB-C: set the nRPIBOOT jumper (GPIO40) before power-on and run rpiboot from the host; mass-storage-gadget64 exposes the Pi's disks as USB mass storage. No boot media or network needed. Untested in conwrt.
rpiboot-usb.requires: physical access, USB-C data cable, host rpiboot package

sd-image.description: Classic SD card flashing (Imager / dd). Boot marker files: 'ssh' (enable sshd), userconf.txt (user), or cloud-init files. Default fallback medium in stock BOOT_ORDER.

netboot_discover.source: Verified on live hardware via router tcpdump, 2026-10-08
netboot_discover.pattern: Repeating DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPOFFER pairs without DHCPREQUEST. Vendor-Class (60) = PXEClient:Arch:00000:UNDI:002001. Parameter request includes TFTP(66), BF(67), 128-135. ARCH(93), NDI(94), GUID(97) with embedded ASCII Rpi4/Rpi5 + MAC suffix.
netboot_discover.meaning: The EEPROM bootloader is network-booting. If these appear while an OS should be installed, the boot medium is missing/dead or BOOT_ORDER prefers network.

no_other_traffic.pattern: Netboot-looping Pi emits NOTHING besides DHCP DISCOVERs — no IPv6 RS, no mDNS, no ARP for a gateway. Presence of any other traffic implies a booted OS.
no_other_traffic.meaning: A Pi showing DHCP-only chatter has never booted an OS. There is no IP to SSH to.

ubuntu_server.sha256: SHA256SUMS in the same directory — always verify
ubuntu_server.headless: cloud-init NoCloud files on the boot FAT partition: user-data (#cloud-config: user, ssh_authorized_keys, hostname), network-config (v2, eth0 dhcp4), meta-data. Inject with scripts/pi_image.py provision or by mounting the boot partition.
ubuntu_server.first_boot: cloud-init grows the rootfs to fill the disk (minutes on large HDDs) and creates the user. sshd is reachable after user creation.
ubuntu_server.note: Ubuntu Server ships with ssh present; verify port 22 after first boot completes. If closed, enable from the rescue shell: symlink ssh.service into multi-user.target.wants in the rootfs.

openwrt.image: OpenWrt bcm27xx/bcm2711 factory image (raspberrypi,4-model-b) written to SD/USB; boot partition carries config.txt + firmware
openwrt.note: OpenWrt on Pi boots the same FAT+ext4 way; use sysupgrade flow only for OpenWrt-on-Pi refreshes.

safety.netboot_security: Plain TFTP netboot is unauthenticated: anyone on the L2 who controls DHCP can boot or re-image a netboot-first Pi. Keep the rescue server DISARMED when not in use (pi_netboot.py disarm), restrict boot options to known MACs (dhcp-host tags), and prefer VLAN port isolation during rescue. True tamper-proofing requires Raspberry Pi secure boot (SIGNED_BOOT=1 + OTP key hash + signed boot.img) — irreversible OTP programming, documented in recipes/raspberry-pi/eeprom-and-security.md.
safety.psu: 2.5in USB HDDs draw ~1A at spin-up. On a weak PSU the Pi browns out mid-boot (hangs, TCP resets, stale ARP). Use externally powered disks or the official 5.1V/3A PSU.
safety.dnsmasq_tftp_hazard: On OpenWrt, dnsmasq runs in a procd ujail: a tftp-root that does not exist (or is outside the jail-mounted conf-dir) crash-loops dnsmasq and takes down LAN DHCP/DNS. Always create the TFTP tree BEFORE configuring, and keep it under /tmp/dnsmasq.<section>.d/ (jail-visible). scripts/pi_netboot.py enforces this ordering with automatic rollback.
safety.no_screen: All rescue paths here work headless: netboot rescue shell (telnetd), cloud-init injection, EEPROM-over-network. UART (BOOT_UART=1) is the last-resort debug channel.

netboot-rescue.notes: Pi 4 4GB netboot-looping on home VLAN (empty SD slot, network-first EEPROM, no netboot server): diagnosed via router tcpdump + dnsmasq verbose log; rescued with dnsmasq TFTP rescue tree (kernel 6.1 + busybox initramfs/telnetd); EEPROM BOOT_ORDER corrected over the same channel.

usb-image.notes: Ubuntu Server 26.04.1 arm64+raspi written to a 1TB USB SSD attached to the Pi, flashed from the netboot rescue shell over LAN (nc transfer, sha256 verified, xzcat|dd, cloud-init injected via built-in kernel vfat). SSD booted Ubuntu natively once. Boot-to-ssh verification was ultimately blocked by a board-level hardware fault on the test unit (memory corruption + spontaneous resets — see recipes/raspberry-pi/netboot-rescue.md RAM diagnostics); the flashing/injection procedure itself is verified.

eeprom-update-netboot.notes: BOOT_ORDER reprogrammed over TFTP-delivered EEPROM package (0xf241 -> 0xf142) and again prepared for LAN-first policy; bootloader version-match skip verified (pieeprom.sig fetched without pieeprom.upd re-download).
